title: Relative open comparison identifies with the literal single-module comparison
statement: Let p:Y→B, g:A→B be arbitrary scheme morphisms, W,Z opens of Y with Z≤W, and N an O_W-module [def-pc-module-pullback]. Use standard derived module categories [def-pc-derived-category]. Put f=W.ι;p, X′=W×_B A, g′=pullback.fst f g, f′=pullback.snd f g, K=N[0], K′=(g′ tensor-pullback N)[0], and φ=picardTermwiseSingleMap(g′,N) [lem-sc-picard-termwise-single-map-composition]. The relative arrow relativeMVLocalArrow f f′ g g′ at the open W.ι inverse image Z [def-pc-relative-mv-maps] is isomorphic in the arrow category to standardSingleBaseChangeMap (Z.ι;p) ((Y.homOfLE hZ) tensor-pullback N) g [def-pc-standard-single-base-change-map]. Both vertex comparisons are invertible; neither comparison arrow is asserted invertible.

proof.text: Set J=W.ι inverse image Z and e=isoOfLE hZ. Cancel the monomorphism W.ι to show e;homOfLE hZ=J.ι, and obtain e;(Z.ι;p)=J.ι;(W.ι;p). Construct e′ by pullbackSymmetry, pullbackRightPullbackFstIso and pullback.map for e. The simp projection equations give k;e=e′;t and e′;s=r;f′. These are concrete scheme isomorphisms, valid also for empty opens.

Prove privately that picardTermwiseSingleMap normalizes to the selected derived counit followed by the localized chain single comparison, by cancellation of the tensor-to-ordinary adjoint uniqueness isomorphism. Restriction along an open immersion preserves limits and colimits; transport exactness through restrictFunctorIsoPullback and leftAdjointUniq to literal tensor pullback. Mathlib isIso_of_isLeftDerivedFunctor_of_inverts makes the selected derived counit invertible. Thus the single comparison is invertible along each open immersion. Construct alpha and beta explicitly from these comparisons, the displayed tensor composition isomorphisms, and the inverse comparisons for J.ι and r. Functoriality and inverse cancellation prove their normalization equations.

Apply single_open_tensor_coefficient_coherence to the two constructed isomorphisms and their proved normalization equations. This supplies only the coefficient compatibility equation, before any direct image or base-change mate.

Apply exists_derivedBaseChange_source_iso to the standard square, e and e′, and the coefficient compatibility. Rewrite the two composite source maps by the proved scheme projection equations. The resulting vertex isomorphisms satisfy the Arrow.isoMk equation. Package their Arrow.isoMk isomorphism and invert it to orient it from the relative local arrow to the standard single comparison.
